tasks.short: Design and deliver disaster preparedness training

steps.what: Define preparedness training objectives and select approved response procedures
Draft emergency training materials from selected procedures

loop.purpose: Organize approved procedures into draft teaching material
loop.input: Training brief and selected procedure versions
loop.output: Draft lesson outline and exercises with source references
loop.check: Resolve procedure identifiers and have the director compare every response instruction with the approved plan and audience needs
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; unsupported instructions are removed and written manually
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle course structure but adapting explanations to the selected audience needs language work

steps.what: Verify course instructions and administer preparedness training with participant practice

tasks.design: Use {DOCS} templates and a bounded assistant to draft from approved response procedures. The director checks exact instructions before delivering training and retains all practical teaching and participant assessment time.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated preparation of explanations and exercises from approved plans.
tasks.enabler_now: Source-grounded drafting can help organize material without choosing emergency actions.
tasks.still_hard: Whether participants can apply instructions under realistic conditions.
tasks.human_edge: The director detects misunderstanding and adjusts the exercise.

reach.learn: Link exercises to observable learning objectives

evidence.claim: The proposed emergency training drafting loop is E1; no measured emergency training product case is provided.

assumptions: Only material drafting changes; practical delivery, exercises and clinical or operational decisions retain full time.

The director produces audience, objective, procedure identifiers, versions and permitted instruction excerpts in s1; 25 hours include capture. Missing or conflicting procedures require manual preparation.
Native templates and reusable approved lessons precede model drafting.
Participant responses arise during s3 practice rather than being assumed available in advance.
research_questions: Can reviewed drafts reduce preparation time while preserving every approved response instruction?

already_counted.description: Source selection, draft checking and practical delivery

incremental.description: Maintain lesson source versions and audit instruction changes

approvals.approved_version: Exact course material version, audience and response instructions; any change requires review before teaching

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=95 gives 5 gross less 3 focal upkeep =2 central net. Report 0-1 until preparation is timed; reused lessons may already remove drafting work.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Track changes affecting emergency likelihood and response

steps.what: Select activities and change sources relevant to emergency planning
Collect matching activities and change notices into a source-linked update list
Assess changes through original notices and direct discussions with response partners

tasks.design: Configure subscriptions and inbox filters in {EMAIL} and the existing update service {OTHER}. The director reads original notices and speaks to partners; the list neither predicts emergencies nor establishes operational readiness.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated manual checking of the same update channels.
tasks.enabler_now: Native subscriptions and filters can gather notices without interpreting their significance.
tasks.still_hard: Incomplete channels, weak signals and deciding whether a change affects response.
tasks.human_edge: The director questions sources and connects changes to local operating conditions.

reach.learn: Check source coverage and verify weak signals directly

evidence.claim: Native update collection is a proposed E1 configuration, not a measured emergency monitoring deployment.

assumptions: This task tracks operational changes; legal rule interpretation belongs to the separate regulatory task.

In s1 the director produces channel identifier, scope, filter terms, delivery frequency and manual fallback owner; 20 hours include capture. Missing notices and failed feeds require direct checking in s3.
OTHER means existing update subscription service; native inbox and source subscriptions precede a custom dashboard.
Partner observations are gathered through s3 discussions with full time retained; no new partner reporting contract is imposed.
research_questions: Does collecting updates through existing subscriptions reduce checking time without missing known relevant changes?

already_counted.description: Source capture, interpretation and partner verification

incremental.description: Maintain subscriptions and test missing-notice coverage

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=80 gives 20 gross less 6 focal upkeep =14 central net. Report 0-3 until channel checking is timed; low case already receives alerts or needs manual verification throughout.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Review emergency plans against actual organizational hazards, resources and response arrangements

tasks.design: Retain adequacy review with the director, using {DOCS} to inspect plans and record concerns. Document completeness is useful context but does not establish that resources and response arrangements will work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Adequacy depends on real capabilities rather than plan wording alone.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing documents and partner discussions support the review.
tasks.still_hard: Unverified resources, conflicting responsibilities and unrealistic response assumptions.
tasks.human_edge: The director challenges apparent readiness and asks for evidence.

reach.learn: Test written arrangements against actual staffing and resources

evidence.claim: Policy platforms such as Clausematch support versions, approvals and rule mappings; that does not establish automated emergency plan adequacy.

assumptions: Reviewing adequacy excludes authoring training materials and routine regulatory monitoring.
The director obtains resource evidence and partner explanations during s1; all capture and verification time remains counted, without a free readiness field.
Existing DOCS suffice before adding a policy platform.
No new automated service or incremental upkeep is introduced.
unknowns: Plan scope and available operational evidence
research_questions: Which plan claims cannot currently be supported by resource or exercise evidence?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100; gross and net saving zero. Policy-record capabilities do not measure adequacy-review labour.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Interpret regulations and align emergency plans

steps.what: Verify current regulations affecting emergency plans and determine local applicability
Review plan adherence and resolve gaps with responsible plan owners

tasks.design: Keep legal applicability and plan adherence review with the director, recording sources and findings in {DOCS}. The US wording requires local scope clarification before applying requirements in the fictional Dutch setting.
tasks.previous_blocker: Regulatory meaning and organizational applicability cannot be inferred from keyword matches.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing source documents and plan reviews support traceable decisions.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting requirements and whether a plan's controls actually satisfy an obligation.
tasks.human_edge: The director explains the interpretation and agrees practical corrective work with owners.

reach.learn: Distinguish source text, applicability and evidence of adherence

evidence.claim: CERRIX offers regulatory monitoring and compliance modules; this supports record handling rather than automatic emergency plan compliance.

assumptions: No specific US or Dutch legal obligation is inferred from the task wording.
The director locates source versions and determines applicability during s1; all time remains counted. Plan-owner explanations are obtained in s2 rather than assumed available beforehand.
Existing DOCS precede a new compliance platform; operational update retrieval savings are assigned to the separate change-tracking task.
No new automation or incremental upkeep is introduced.
research_questions: Which source versions and scope decisions currently underpin each emergency plan requirement?

already_counted.description: Source verification, applicability judgment and plan adherence review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 gives zero gross and net saving; operational update retrieval is not counted again here.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Operational emergency preparedness and accountable plan judgment
reach: Learn practical teaching design from instructional coordinators
Coordinate with compliance and facility leaders on evidence for plans
role.ambitious_version: A director who gathers routine updates efficiently while retaining direct responsibility for plans, interpretation and realistic preparedness
